answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake that unlocks slowly, like dawn breaking over a river: the stake vests only after the agent completes verified work for independent peers, so a fake identity costs real locked capital and time. Sybils created at scale drain the attacker's funds, since each one must still perform real work before earning anything, while a jetty-like gate — only agents vouched for by two established, uncorrelated peers may enter new markets — pushes the marginal cost of each additional fake identity above its expected gain.
